open_issues: Wakeel.Design's WButton renders its Tooltip parameter only for the Icon variant; for every other variant the text never reaches the DOM. A03's two switched-off controls therefore had to be wrapped in WTooltip by hand to say why they will not open. Wakeel.Design is outside this package's paths, so nothing was changed there — but the other packages' Refresh/ExportSetup-style tooltips on labelled buttons are silently dropped everywhere in the tool, and that belongs to whoever owns Wakeel.Design.

Another agent modified src/Wakeel.Design/Components/WInput.razor and src/Wakeel.Design/wwwroot/js/app.js in the same working tree while this package was building. All builds here used --no-dependencies, so admin-1 was compiled and tested against the Wakeel.Design assembly as it stood; a full solution build after that package lands should be re-run by whoever integrates.
notes:
All findings of docs/build/reviews/B1/verify2-admin-1.json applied; build green (0 warnings under TreatWarningsAsErrors) for Wakeel.Admin.UI, Wakeel.Admin and the tests, 75/75 tests passing (64 before, 11 new).

MEDIUM — admin.key.bak keeping a superseded password wrap. AdminKeyFile.Save now takes an explicit `keepBackup` choice (default true, documented as «only while the wraps are unchanged»); when false it skips the copy and deletes any existing backup after the new file is in place (TryDeleteBackup, try/catch IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException). AdminAccountService.Create() and Recover() both save with keepBackup:false and then call the new RemoveRetiredKeyFileBackup(), the same discipline TryDeleteDatabase() uses. New test Recover_LeavesNothingOnDiskThatTheOldPasswordStillOpens: a wrong password first forces a real admin.key.bak into existence, recovery then runs, the backup is asserted gone, and every file under keys\ is loaded and every password wrap in it proven to refuse GoodPassword and to open with the new one. Second test Create_LeavesNoBackupBesideTheBrandNewKeyFile. Confirmed on the live host: keys\ held admin.key alone after a first run.

MISSING ITEM — the lock-out left no audit row. AdminKeyFile gained LockOutsToReport (incremented in RecordWrongPassword where the database is necessarily shut, cleared in ClearAttempts and in Recover). SignIn() and Recover() capture it before clearing and WriteServedLockOuts() writes one «admin.signin.lockedout» row per served lock-out with AdminAr.AccountAudit.LockedOut once the database is open. Two tests: two rounds of five wrong passwords produce exactly two rows and a further sign-in adds none; a lock-out served before a recovery is still written.

LOW — A01 exit guard. Exit() routes through AdminConfirmDialog (Danger, RequireTypedConfirmation="false") whenever the sheet is on screen and the tick box is empty; confirming clears the copied code from the clipboard and then closes. Three new Arabic strings (ExitUnsavedTitle/Desc/Confirm/Cancel). Two bUnit tests using a new TestAdminWindow that counts closes: pressing «الخروج» with an unconfirmed sheet opens the dialog and closes nothing, cancelling leaves the sheet, confirming closes once; with the box ticked it closes straight away.

LOW — A03 dead controls. The two routes are read once in OnInitialized; while AdminRoutes has no route, «تصدير ملف الإعداد» and «عرض الكل» render Disabled inside a WTooltip saying «هذا الجزء غير متاح في هذه النسخة بعد.» (new AdminAr.Dashboard.NotReadyYetTooltip). Test asserts both buttons carry the disabled attribute and the bubble text.

LOW — A01 MachineLine now reads AdminOptions.MachineName (injected as A02 does), with a test pinning it to the test context's name.

LOW — the strength meter shows «—» while the password box is empty instead of judging it «قصيرة جدًا»; the four rule lines are untouched. Test asserts the empty-password verdict is absent before typing and present after.

LOW — dashboard counting rule, chosen and written down: an office counts only while the unit it hangs from and every unit above it is in service, and a device counts only while its office does. Two SQL fragments (FromLiveOffices/FromLiveDevices) walk the three possible ancestors and are reused by the office, activated-office, device and revoked-device counts, by both alert queries, and by the last-export read, so the cards, the alerts panel, the structure summary and «آخر تصدير» can never name a branch the board no longer draws. The rule is stated in full on AdminDashboard.Offices for admin-2 to inherit. Two tests: disabling a department removes its office and its waiting alert, disabling the one above removes the devices, the revoked-device alert and the last export; a second test proves an office two layers below a disabled department goes too.

LOW — deleted AdminAr.Account.SignIn.WrongPassword, AdminAr.Account.Create.SheetOrgLabel and AdminAr.Dashboard.StructureEmptyAction.

HOST RUN. Wakeel.Admin.exe launched from bin with --remote-debugging-port=9334 --window-size=1366x768 --data-folder=<temp> --start-url=/first-run; /json/version answered (Edg/152.0.4191.66).
